question: Assume today is 2026-10-27. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of UK residential property transactions (with a value of £40,000 or above) in September 2026, seasonally adjusted, as it will be first reported (provisional estimate) in HM Revenue & Customs' monthly release 'Monthly property transactions completed in the UK with value of £40,000 or above'.

target.what: Number of completed residential property transactions in the UK with a value of £40,000 or above in September 2026, seasonally adjusted, as first reported (provisional estimate) in HMRC's monthly property transactions release.
target.caveats: Target is HMRC's headline residential seasonally adjusted count for the UK, not non-residential transactions, mortgage approvals, SDLT receipts, or transactions below £40,000. The target period is complete at the information cutoff, but the first provisional publication may occur after 2026-10-27 an

candidates.perspective: HMRC statistical release and time-series analyst
candidates.hypothesis: The September 2026 first provisional estimate should be anchored by recent seasonally adjusted HMRC residential transaction levels and the historical September seasonal pattern; the role of own history is to set the base level and seasonal adjustment, with expected direction from recent trend and prior Septembers. Transfer assumption: the seasonal pattern and reporting lags remain broadly stable.
candidates.data_to_find: HMRC monthly property transactions table for residential, seasonally adjusted, UK: observations for September 2018-2025 and latest months through August 2026; first provisional versus latest revised values for September months; published seasonal adjustment factors. Minimum evidence: 12-24 months of seasonally adjusted residential monthly counts plus historical September observations.
search_hints: HMRC property transactions September 2025 seasonally adjusted residential
site:gov.uk monthly property transactions completed UK £40,000 September 2026
HMRC property transactions table monthly residential seasonally adjusted 2026

candidates.perspective: Bank of England / mortgage market analyst
candidates.hypothesis: Mortgage approvals for house purchase lead completed property transactions by roughly 1-3 months, so approvals around June-August 2026 should help predict September 2026 completions, with cash purchases and variable lags breaking exact proportionality. Higher prior approvals imply higher September completions, all else equal.
candidates.data_to_find: Bank of England Money and Credit mortgage approvals for house purchase, seasonally adjusted, UK, for June-August 2026 and historical relationship to HMRC completions; UK Finance or HMRC cash-buyer share to add non-mortgage transactions. Minimum evidence: approvals series and a historical lag/ratio benchmark.
search_hints: Bank of England mortgage approvals house purchase August 2026
UK Finance mortgage completions September 2026
cash buyer share UK property transactions 2026

candidates.perspective: Housing market survey and listings analyst
candidates.hypothesis: Newly agreed sales and sales pipelines 1-3 months before completion should move in the same direction as September 2026 completions; use as a directional adjustment or check on the trend because coverage and timing differ from HMRC counts. Stronger prior sales agreed imply stronger September completions.
candidates.data_to_find: RICS residential market survey sales agreed and sales expectations for June-August 2026; Rightmove or Zoopla sales-agreed/pipeline indicators for mid-2026; historical correlation with HMRC monthly completions at a 1-3 month lag. Minimum evidence: one consistent UK-wide sales-agreed/pipeline series covering mid-2026.
search_hints: RICS residential market survey August 2026 sales agreed
Rightmove sales agreed August 2026 UK
Zoopla sales pipeline September 2026

candidates.perspective: Devolved tax authority and land transaction administrative data analyst
candidates.hypothesis: The UK total can be approximated by summing administrative residential transaction counts from England/Northern Ireland SDLT, Scotland LBTT, and Wales LTT, then adjusting for the £40,000 threshold and seasonal adjustment. If administrative counts are available near September 2026, they directly constrain the unadjusted target.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly or quarterly residential transaction counts from HMRC SDLT statistics for England/Northern Ireland, Revenue Scotland LBTT statistics, and Welsh Revenue Authority LTT statistics around September 2026; thresholds, coverage, and publication lag. Minimum evidence: counts covering at least a recent comparable period or September 2026 partials.
search_hints: Revenue Scotland LBTT monthly statistics September 2026
Welsh Revenue Authority LTT monthly transactions 2026
HMRC SDLT monthly property transactions England Northern Ireland 2026

candidates.perspective: Housing market forecaster and annual-to-monthly bridge analyst
candidates.hypothesis: A published 2026 UK residential transaction forecast multiplied by the historical September share of annual transactions should provide an independent level check for the monthly target. The forecast must match HMRC's residential £40,000+ definition, and the September share must be stable enough to transfer.
candidates.data_to_find: Published 2026 UK residential property transaction forecasts from Savills, Zoopla, Hamptons, RICS, or OBR before the cutoff; HMRC historical September share of annual residential transactions for 2018-2025. Minimum evidence: one annual 2026 forecast with a defined transaction scope and a historical September share.
search_hints: UK residential property transactions forecast 2026 Savills
Zoopla UK housing transactions 2026 forecast
HMRC September share annual property transactions

candidates.hypothesis: The first provisional HMRC estimate may differ from later revised data because of late returns and seasonal adjustment; the historical revision distribution for September constrains how the first print relates to a trend-based estimate. The expected direction is toward the typical first-print bias for September, if any.
candidates.data_to_find: HMRC first provisional and latest revised seasonally adjusted residential monthly counts by month for 2018-2025; September-specific revision averages and recent revision patterns. Minimum evidence: matched first and revised observations for several Septembers.
search_hints: HMRC property transactions revisions provisional revised
monthly property transactions statistics revisions table HMRC
HMRC property transactions first provisional September revision

candidates.hypothesis: Mortgage-financed house purchase completions for September 2026 plus an estimated cash share should reconstruct total residential transactions; this is a direct flow bridge if UK Finance or lender data are available. Coverage differences and the cash share stability are the key transfer assumptions.
candidates.data_to_find: UK Finance number of house purchase mortgage completions for September 2026 or Q3 2026; cash share of UK residential transactions from HMRC, English Housing Survey, or industry sources; historical alignment between UK Finance completions and HMRC transaction counts. Minimum evidence: a recent mortgage-completions count and a defensible cash share.
search_hints: UK Finance house purchase completions September 2026
UK Finance mortgage market forecast 2026 completions
cash share residential property transactions UK 2025

candidates.perspective: Macro, policy, and calendar effects analyst
candidates.hypothesis: Mortgage-rate changes, tax-threshold or stamp-duty policy changes, and September 2026 working-day patterns could shift completion timing relative to the recent trend. The role is to identify whether September 2026 had unusual measurable exposure that should adjust a trend-based estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Bank of England Bank Rate decisions and average mortgage rates through September 2026; stamp duty, LBTT, or LTT policy changes effective in 2026; UK working days and holidays in September 2026; relevant housing-market news before the cutoff. Minimum evidence: confirmation that no major policy change or unusual calendar effect distorted September 2026, or a measurable adjustment.
search_hints: Bank Rate September 2026
stamp duty land tax changes 2026 residential
UK bank holidays September 2026 working days

assessment.note: These are HMRC residential transaction values from one underlying administrative source, often repeated by multiple outlets. They establish the recent SA level around 95-97k, the September 2025 SA level of 95,980, and NSA September 2025 of 102,420. Duplicates are one source, not independent confirmation.

July 2026 first provisional SA estimate was 96,710, while the latest HMRC release reports 96,650. The small downward revision shows first prints can differ from settled values; latest vintage should be used for levels, initial vintage only for revision context.

Bank of England mortgage approvals weakened into summer 2026: August 54,900, revised July 55,900, June 58,200, well below the roughly 60,100 six-month average. These are near-duplicates from the same BoE source and point to softer September completions.

Scottish administrative evidence points to weaker activity: September 2026 LBTT residential returns 9,010, down 9% yoy; July-August returns down 5.7% yoy; Q2 2026 Scottish sales down 2.1% yoy. Measures are related but not identical.

Annual UK transaction forecasts and long-run levels cluster around 1.18-1.21 million: UK Finance 1,202,000 for 2026 and 1,210,000 for 2025; Zoopla 1.18m; long-run average around 1.2m. Definitions and forecast vintages differ.
RICS survey balances remained negative but improved from spring lows. They are directional evidence only and are repeated across outlets from the same survey.

HMRC-related documentation says offer-to-completion is typically two to four months, while another market commentary cites sales reported in a different dataset as agreed five to six months earlier. Different datasets and definitions, so not a direct contradiction, but it widens lag uncertainty.

p490 reports July 2026 NSA UK transactions as 107,610, while HMRC-derived reports give 106,620. The latter is corroborated by multiple outlets and is the consistent July NSA value; p490 appears an outlier or different vintage.
September 2025 HMRC SA 95,980 and NSA 102,420 imply a September SA/NSA factor near 0.937. The reported 1% SA rise and 2% NSA fall versus August 2025 are consistent with those levels.

methods.rationale: Use the target's own SA HMRC history. Latest months are June-August 2026 at 98,390, 96,650 and 95,220; September 2025 was 95,980 and August 2025 was 97,040. The recent YoY declines of roughly 1-2% imply a September 2026 level modestly below September 2025, while the library also considers recent momentum. Main risk: sparse monthly coverage and revision of the latest vintages.

methods.rationale: Approvals lead completions by roughly one to three months, so June-August 2026 approvals are the relevant pipeline. The ratio p1/p85 converts current approvals into HMRC SA transaction equivalents, absorbing cash purchases and approval-to-completion attrition. Risk: the ratio may vary with timing and cash share; using the August same-month ratio for a September lead relationship is a transfer assumption.

methods.rationale: Independent annual-level check: apply September 2025's SA share of the 2025 annual transaction total to the UK Finance 2026 forecast. It assumes the September seasonal share is stable and that the annual forecast is consistent with HMRC's GBP 40,000+ residential definition. Main risk: the annual forecast is not an actual HMRC outturn and September share can shift.

assessment.note: Consistent HMRC seasonally adjusted residential transaction series, same definition and unit. They set the recent level around the mid-90,000s and provide prior Septembers for seasonal/own-history comparison. p1 is the latest provisional August anchor; p3 is a later revised July value than earlier-vintage July prints.

Bank of England net mortgage approvals for house purchase are weakening in summer 2026, with August below the six-month average. These are approvals, not completions, and are used only through a lag/ratio bridge. Minor vintage differences such as p115 versus p86 are not material contradictions.

Scottish administrative/LBTT evidence points to weaker September residential activity, especially the -9% year-on-year LBTT returns, while annual Scottish sales to June 2026 were still slightly up. The periods differ, so these are not contradictory but they do not give a direct UK September count without scaling.

RICS survey balances indicate agreed sales remained negative but were improving from the April low. This is directional evidence for a soft market, not a level for HMRC completions, because survey balances are not transaction counts.

Annual UK housing transaction forecasts cluster around 1.18-1.20 million for 2026, with UK Finance around 1.20 million. They are forecasts, not realised outcomes, and are used only as a level check through a historical September share.

September 2025 HMRC estimates are internally consistent: seasonally adjusted about 95,980 and non-seasonally adjusted about 102,420. Duplicates come from different publications of the same underlying release.

July 2026 seasonally adjusted HMRC values appear as about 96,710 in earlier provisional coverage and 96,650 in the later vintage. This is a small revision/vintage difference, not a substantive contradiction; methods should use the later vintage p3.

August 2026 month-on-month seasonally adjusted change is reported as about 1.5% by one secondary source and 1% by HMRC-derived coverage. The difference is rounding/vintage and does not change the level evidence.

Cash-buyer shares differ widely: about 35% in Hamptons/GB 2026 evidence, about 25% in another UK 2026 source, and about 20% in Zoopla's earlier sales mix. These reflect different definitions, years and populations, so they should not be averaged mechanically; none is used as a direct numerical target input.

Mortgage-rate evidence consistently indicates elevated new-mortgage rates in 2026, supporting the weak approvals/RICS picture. Rate levels are context for demand and timing, not direct transaction counts.
Scotland September 2026 LBTT returns and year-ending-June 2026 sales are different period/scope measures. The annual sales figure can only be used as a scaling denominator, not as a September level.

methods.rationale: Own-history route for the seasonally adjusted HMRC target. It uses the latest available monthly seasonally adjusted HMRC values, including June-August 2026, plus prior Septembers and nearby August levels. The series is sparse, so the method relies mainly on last year's September value and the recent year-on-year/monthly trend. It shares the HMRC definitions and is the most direct target-history route.

p1.role: UK residential transactions, seasonally adjusted, August 2026 HMRC provisional estimate

p101.role: UK net mortgage approvals for house purchase, seasonally adjusted, June 2026

p86.role: UK net mortgage approvals for house purchase, seasonally adjusted, July 2026

p85.role: UK net mortgage approvals for house purchase, seasonally adjusted, August 2026

p118.role: UK net mortgage approvals for house purchase, seasonally adjusted, May 2026

a3.role: dimensionless adjustment for September 2026 transaction-to-approval ratio relative to August 2026

methods.rationale: Mortgage-approvals bridge. August 2026 completions are paired with approvals from roughly May-July, while September completions are paired with approvals from June-August. The observed August transaction-to-approval relationship captures the cash share and approval-to-completion gap; a3 allows small drift. It is independent of the pure HMRC own-history route but shares the soft approvals signal and cannot capture cash-only or policy-driven timing shifts.

p210.role: Revenue Scotland LBTT residential returns, September 2026, administrative count

p333.role: UK Finance forecast of total UK housing transactions in 2026, annual level used as UK scale

p235.role: Residential property sales in Scotland, year ending June 2026, annual level

p56.role: UK residential transactions, seasonally adjusted, September 2025 HMRC provisional estimate

p18.role: UK residential transactions, non-seasonally adjusted, September 2025 HMRC estimate

a1.role: dimensionless factor for September Scotland share relative to annual Scotland share

methods.rationale: Administrative Scotland-to-UK route. Scottish September 2026 LBTT residential returns directly observe completed residential activity near the target month. The annual Scotland share from p235/p333 scales to a UK unadjusted total, and p56/p18 converts the September 2025 non-seasonally adjusted level to the HMRC seasonally adjusted basis. a1 handles September-vs-annual Scotland share differences. Key failure modes are use of a forecast UK annual total and divergence between Scottish and UK September markets.

p333.role: UK Finance forecast of total UK housing transactions in 2026, annual level

p56.role: UK residential transactions, seasonally adjusted, September 2025 HMRC provisional estimate

p350.role: UK property transactions in 2025, UK Finance annual estimate

a2.role: dimensionless adjustment for September 2026 annual share relative to September 2025 share

methods.rationale: Annual-forecast level check. It multiplies the 2026 UK Finance annual transaction forecast by the September 2025 seasonally adjusted share of the 2025 annual total. a2 allows the September share to drift slightly. This route is independent of the monthly HMRC trajectory but depends on an annual forecast and on stability of the September share; it does not use the recent approvals weakness directly.

assumptions.name: September Scotland share of UK residential transactions relative to annual share
assumptions.rationale: The Scotland-to-UK scaling uses the annual Scottish sales share from p235/p333. Scotland's September LBTT returns may not equal its annual share because of seasonality and market mix, so a dimensionless adjustment around 1 is needed. The Scottish September evidence is weaker than the annual sales trend, but no direct September UK/Scotland share is available.
assumptions.applies_when: Used only when scaling p210 Scotland September LBTT returns to a UK September estimate using the annual Scotland share p235/p333.
assumptions.falsified_by: Published UK and Scotland September 2026 transaction counts implying a Scotland September share outside 0.9-1.1 times the annual share.

assumptions.name: September 2026 share of annual UK transactions relative to September 2025 share
assumptions.rationale: The annual-forecast route applies the September 2025 SA share of annual transactions, p56/p350, to the 2026 UK Finance forecast p333. The September share is usually stable, but 2026 activity and mortgage conditions could shift it slightly, so a dimensionless adjustment around 1 is appropriate.
assumptions.applies_when: Used when converting the 2026 annual transaction forecast to a September 2026 monthly estimate through the prior-year September share.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026's share of 2026 annual transactions is outside 0.95-1.05 times the September 2025 share.

assumptions.name: September 2026 transaction-to-approval ratio relative to August 2026
assumptions.rationale: The approvals bridge uses August 2026 HMRC transactions relative to May-July approvals and applies the June-August approvals level. The total-transaction-to-approval ratio includes cash purchases and approval-to-completion timing; it is likely stable over one month but can drift with rates and cash share, so a narrow dimensionless adjustment is allowed.
assumptions.applies_when: Used when projecting September 2026 completions from Bank of England approvals around June-August 2026 using the August 2026 observed transaction/approval relationship.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a material one-month shift in cash-buyer share or in approval-to-completion timing not captured by the approvals series.

final.template:
The best estimate for UK residential property transactions of £[n] or above, seasonally adjusted, in September 2026, as first provisionally reported by HMRC, is [[estimate]] [[unit]] ([[interval_level]] interval [[p10]] to [[p90]] [[unit]]).

The combination is the median of four equally weighted blocks. The own-history route ([[m1_estimate]] [[unit]], weight [[m1_weight]]) carries last year's September level ([[p56_value]]) forward with recent year-on-year growth. The approvals bridge ([[m2_estimate]] [[unit]]) links August completions ([[p1_value]]) to June–August approvals ([[p101_value]], [[p86_value]], [[p85_value]]). The Scotland route ([[m3_estimate]] [[unit]]) scales September LBTT returns ([[p210_value]]) to the UK. The annual-forecast check ([[m4_estimate]] [[unit]]) applies the September share to the UK Finance 2026 forecast ([[p333_value]]).

Observed inputs are the HMRC months, approvals, LBTT returns and annual figures; the scaling adjustments ([[a1_value]], [[a2_value]], [[a3_value]]) are assumptions. The interval is conditional on these assumptions, not a demonstrated accuracy guarantee. The main risk is that the sparse HMRC series and weak approvals signal misstate the recent trend; more timely completions data would help most.

Unit of the estimate: [[unit_full]].

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 September Scotland share of UK residential transactions relative to annual share: [[a1_value]] [n], range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]] (range widened by code); used by m3. Overturned by: Published UK and Scotland September 2026 transaction counts implying a Scotland September share outside [n]-[n] times the annual share.
- a2 September 2026 share of annual UK transactions relative to September 2025 share: [[a2_value]] [n], range [[a2_low]] to [[a2_high]] (range widened by code); used by m4. Overturned by: Evidence that September 2026's share of 2026 annual transactions is outside [n]-[n] times the September 2025 share.
- a3 September 2026 transaction-to-approval ratio relative to August 2026: [[a3_value]] [n], range [[a3_low]] to [[a3_high]] (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence of a material one-month shift in cash-buyer share or in approval-to-completion timing not captured by the approvals series.

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 series_auto, yoy path: yoy2: last year's same month x the summed growth of the latest 2 year-on-year pairs. Members: yoy2 [[m1_yoy2]] (base month [[m1_yoy2_base]] = [[m1_yoy2_base_value]] x growth [[m1_yoy2_growth]] over [[m1_yoy2_pairs]] year-on-year pair(s): sum of these months / sum of the same months a year earlier, [[m1_yoy2_pair_values]]). Data window [[m1_window]] ([[m1_n_months]] months used, not consecutive; last month [[m1_last_month]], [[m1_h]] month(s) before the target; the run of consecutive months ending there is [[m1_consecutive]] long). Calibrated 80% interval [[m1_p10]] to [[m1_p90]]; own 80% width [[m1_width]] (benchmark calibration, row [[m1_row]] of table [[m1_table]])
- m2 formula_mc: p1 * mean(p101, p86, p85) / mean(p118, p101, p86) * a3; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m2_mc_p10]] to [[m2_mc_p90]]; result unit (transaction/month) * 1 month converted to transaction; own 80% width [[m2_width]] (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- m3 formula_mc: p210 * (p333 / p235) * (p56 / p18) * a1; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m3_mc_p10]] to [[m3_mc_p90]]; result unit (transaction/month) * 1 month converted to transaction; own 80% width [[m3_width]] (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- m4 formula_mc: p333 * p56 / p350 * a2; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m4_mc_p10]] to [[m4_mc_p90]]; result unit (transaction/month) * 1 month converted to transaction; own 80% width [[m4_width]] (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- Combination: [[n_blocks]] block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: [[block1_value]] (width [[block1_width]], benchmark calibration); B2 = m2: [[block2_value]] (width [[block2_width]], Monte Carlo of the formula inputs); B3 = m3: [[block3_value]] (width [[block3_width]], Monte Carlo of the formula inputs); B4 = m4: [[block4_value]] (width [[block4_width]], Monte Carlo of the formula inputs). Estimate = the median of the blocks.
- Interval: root mean square of the block widths [[blocks_rms_width]]; Birge ratio [[birge_ratio]] (not above one, so no widening); final width [[final_width]].
- Seasonal naive baseline (not combined): [[baseline]] ([[baseline_period]], point p56, from m1); the estimate is [[baseline_diff]] against it.
final.text:
The best estimate for UK residential property transactions of £[n] or above, seasonally adjusted, in September 2026, as first provisionally reported by HMRC, is 94,743 transaction (80% model-based interval 62,382 to 143,890 transaction).

The combination is the median of four equally weighted blocks. The own-history route (94,507 transaction, weight 50%) carries last year's September level (95,980 transaction) forward with recent year-on-year growth. The approvals bridge (94,248 transaction) links August completions (95,220 transaction) to June–August approvals (58,200 transaction, 55,900 transaction, 54,900 transaction). The Scotland route (97,336 transaction) scales September LBTT returns (9,010 residential return) to the UK. The annual-forecast check (94,979 transaction) applies the September share to the UK Finance 2026 forecast (1,200,000 transaction).

Observed inputs are the HMRC months, approvals, LBTT returns and annual figures; the scaling adjustments (1, 1, 1) are assumptions. The interval is conditional on these assumptions, not a demonstrated accuracy guarantee. The main risk is that the sparse HMRC series and weak approvals signal misstate the recent trend; more timely completions data would help most.

Unit of the estimate: transaction (total for 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30).

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 September Scotland share of UK residential transactions relative to annual share: 1 [n], range 0.7036 to 1.407 (range widened by code); used by m3. Overturned by: Published UK and Scotland September 2026 transaction counts implying a Scotland September share outside [n]-[n] times the annual share.
- a2 September 2026 share of annual UK transactions relative to September 2025 share: 1 [n], range 0.7062 to 1.412 (range widened by code); used by m4. Overturned by: Evidence that September 2026's share of 2026 annual transactions is outside [n]-[n] times the September 2025 share.
- a3 September 2026 transaction-to-approval ratio relative to August 2026: 1 [n], range 0.7062 to 1.412 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence of a material one-month shift in cash-buyer share or in approval-to-completion timing not captured by the approvals series.

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 series_auto, yoy path: yoy2: last year's same month x the summed growth of the latest 2 year-on-year pairs. Members: yoy2 94,507 (base month 2025-09 = 95,980 x growth 0.9847 over 2 year-on-year pair(s): sum of these months / sum of the same months a year earlier, 2026-07: 96,650 / 97,820; 2026-08: 95,220 / 97,040). Data window 2025-07 (p34), 2025-08 (p4), 2025-09 (p56), 2026-07 (p3), 2026-08 (p1) (5 months used, not consecutive; last month 2026-08, 1 month(s) before the target; the run of consecutive months ending there is 3 long). Calibrated 80% interval 79,341 to 114,815; own 80% width x/÷1.20 (benchmark calibration, row yoy|pairs2|h1 of table bench-d12f86e0-1013c974)
- m2 formula_mc: p1 * mean(p101, p86, p85) / mean(p118, p101, p86) * a3; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 63,457 to 140,758; result unit (transaction/month) * 1 month converted to transaction; own 80% width x/÷1.49 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- m3 formula_mc: p210 * (p333 / p235) * (p56 / p18) * a1; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 56,907 to 165,021; result unit (transaction/month) * 1 month converted to transaction; own 80% width x/÷1.70 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- m4 formula_mc: p333 * p56 / p350 * a2; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 59,443 to 152,633; result unit (transaction/month) * 1 month converted to transaction; own 80% width x/÷1.60 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- Combination: 4 block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: 94,507 (width x/÷1.20, benchmark calibration); B2 = m2: 94,248 (width x/÷1.49, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs); B3 = m3: 97,336 (width x/÷1.70, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs); B4 = m4: 94,979 (width x/÷1.60, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs). Estimate = the median of the blocks.
- Interval: root mean square of the block widths x/÷1.52; Birge ratio 0.04 (not above one, so no widening); final width x/÷1.52.
- Seasonal naive baseline (not combined): 95,980 (2025-09, point p56, from m1); the estimate is -1.3% against it.

placeholders.interval_basis: several routes with separate inputs: the width is the typical width of the routes' own intervals, not narrowed for their number

final.model_text:
The best estimate for UK residential property transactions of £40,000 or above, seasonally adjusted, in September 2026, as first provisionally reported by HMRC, is [[estimate]] [[unit]] ([[interval_level]] interval [[p10]] to [[p90]] [[unit]]).

The combination is the median of four equally weighted blocks. The own-history route ([[m1_estimate]] [[unit]], weight [[m1_weight]]) carries last year's September level ([[p56_value]]) forward with recent year-on-year growth. The approvals bridge ([[m2_estimate]] [[unit]]) links August completions ([[p1_value]]) to June–August approvals ([[p101_value]], [[p86_value]], [[p85_value]]). The Scotland route ([[m3_estimate]] [[unit]]) scales September LBTT returns ([[p210_value]]) to the UK. The annual-forecast check ([[m4_estimate]] [[unit]]) applies the September share to the UK Finance 2026 forecast ([[p333_value]]).

Observed inputs are the HMRC months, approvals, LBTT returns and annual figures; the scaling adjustments ([[a1_value]], [[a2_value]], [[a3_value]]) are assumptions. The interval is conditional on these assumptions, not a demonstrated accuracy guarantee. The main risk is that the sparse HMRC series and weak approvals signal misstate the recent trend; more timely completions data would help most.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
